title: preserveNulls(false) converts a present null into an absent key, silently voiding the absent-vs-null guarantee
rationale: "An absent key is distinct from a present null" is asserted unconditionally. It is not unconditional: one builder flag turns it off, and the Javadoc never mentions that disabling it destroys a documented fidelity property. This is the synthetic-violation arm for the null domain.
catchesBugClass: A default flip on preserveNulls, and an implementation where the flag is honoured inconsistently - respected at the top level but ignored inside reconstructArray.
cannotCatch: Only exercises a null at depth 2 in an object. It does not cover a null ELEMENT inside a reconstructed array, where dropping the entry changes element identity rather than key presence.

predicted.detail: The present key is gone entirely, not nulled. Defensible because it is explicitly opt-in and the sparse-output use case is legitimate; what is not defensible is the silence in the documentation.

configDescription: JsonReconstructor.builder().preserveNulls(false); probe asserts the default run DIFFERS

probe.note: preserveNulls(false) vs the default must produce different documents - that difference proves the control is live
